prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a foreground kitchen layout that opens into a deep living room background (over 4–5 metres away, shown in near-black), with a stainless-steel refrigerator on the left at 0.5–0.8 metres and a kitchen island behind the people at roughly 1.5–2.5 metres. In frames 1–3, the camera wearer's own left arm (bottom-left, ~0.3–0.4 metres, bright white) points at a flyer held within arm's reach (~0.4–0.5 metres) by a first person standing immediately to the right (~0.3–0.5 metres, partly cropped at the right edge and facing left toward the flyer), while a second person in a dark top stands just behind and to the left of the first person at ~1.0–1.3 metres (~0.6 metres from the first person) facing toward the foreground before turning toward the refrigerator in frames 4–5. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer turns and moves slightly closer to the refrigerator as the second person steps forward to ~0.9–1.1 metres, reaches out to pull the refrigerator door open toward the right, and shifts rightward as the open door occludes the background counter. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the overlapping foreground layers—distinguishing the wearer's pointing arm, the flyer, the first person's torso, the second person behind them, and the recessed shelves inside the open fridge—without being confused by specular reflections on the stainless-steel door. However, the map is unreliable on the flat floor plane (which shows a steep brightness gradient), blurs fine finger boundaries, and flattens everything in the distant living room beyond 3 metres into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies discrete objects and people across the kitchen and background living room, labeling the foreground stainless-steel refrigerator on the left (only in frame 5 at ~0.5 metres), bottles (~0.7–1.5 metres), a cup (~2 metres), potted plants on the counter (~1.8–2.5 metres) and in the background (~4–5 metres), a distant TV and wall clock (~5–6 metres), and up to three person regions. In frames 1 and 3, it segments the camera wearer's own pointing left arm at the bottom-left (~0.3–0.4 metres) separately from the two people on the right: a near person in a grey jacket at ~0.3–0.5 metres (holding the flyer within arm's reach and facing left) and a second person in a dark shirt standing just behind them at ~1.0–1.3 metres (within ~0.6 metres of the first person, facing left/front before reaching left to open the fridge door in frames 4–5 and stepping to the right edge). Unlike the RGB image, the segmentation masks isolate small distant background classes (such as the wall clock, TV, cup, and potted plants) and delineate the silhouette of the reaching arm against the dark countertop in frame 4. However, the map is highly unreliable across frames: it completely misses the refrigerator in frames 1–4 and the held paper flyer in all frames, drops the camera wearer's arm entirely in frames 2, 4, and 5, and inconsistently merges or swaps the masks of the two people on the right (fusing both into single or overlapping masks in frames 2, 4, and 5 as the nearer person is partially occluded at the right frame boundary).
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely black and fails to capture the scene layout, objects, or any full-body spatial relationships across the first four frames, detecting only two isolated, partial skeletons in frames 3 and 5. In frame 3, a magenta hand skeleton appears in the lower-center foreground at roughly 0.4–0.5 metres from the camera wearer, corresponding to the left hand of the person standing on the right (~0.3–0.5 metres away) gripping the right edge of the flyer within arm's reach of both that person and the camera wearer's pointing hand (~0.15 metres to the left). In frame 5, a partial yellow body skeleton appears at the far right edge at roughly 0.9–1.1 metres from the camera wearer, tracking the head/face keypoints (facing left toward the open refrigerator door, not looking at the camera wearer), extended right shoulder-elbow-wrist chain reaching left to hold the fridge door handle, and hip line of the person in the dark shirt. While this map explicitly localizes the articulated finger joints gripping the flyer in frame 3 and the exact shoulder-to-wrist reach geometry and head orientation in frame 5 that are dark or motion-blurred in the RGB strip, it is severely unreliable overall because it misses all body and hand poses in frames 1, 2, and 4, never detects the camera wearer's foreground hand, and omits the nearer person's body in every frame due to heavy truncation and occlusion at the image edges.
